notes: Run these when shell/subagent access is available. In the current sandbox bash, web, and subagent tools were blocked, so the quantitative with-skill vs baseline loop and description-optimization loop could not be executed. Each prompt below should yield a runnable .jmx; assertions check structural correctness because JMeter silently mis-loads malformed plans.

evals.prompt: Make a JMeter load test for https://shop.example.com : 200 concurrent users for 5 minutes, ramping up over a minute, hitting GET /api/products?category=shoes and expecting HTTP 200. Add a summary report.
evals.expected_output: A .jmx with one Thread Group (num_threads=200, ramp_time=60, scheduler=true, duration=300, loops=-1), an HTTPSamplerProxy GET /api/products with category=shoes as an HTTPArgument, a ResponseAssertion on response_code equals 200, and a SummaryReport ResultCollector.

assertions.name: well_formed_xml
assertions.text: Output parses as well-formed XML with root <jmeterTestPlan>.

assertions.name: time_bounded
assertions.text: ThreadGroup.scheduler is true, duration is 300, and LoopController.loops is -1.

assertions.name: query_param
assertions.text: The products sampler carries category=shoes as an HTTPArgument with use_equals=true.

assertions.name: hashtree_consistent
assertions.text: Every test element is followed by exactly one hashTree (builder structural check passes).

evals.prompt: I need a jmeter scenario that logs in via POST /auth/login with a JSON body {email,password}, grabs the access_token from the JSON response, then calls GET /orders with that token as a Bearer header. 50 users, 200 iterations each, against api.example.com over https.
evals.expected_output: A .jmx with a Thread Group (threads=50, loops=200, scheduler=false), a POST /auth/login sampler with a raw JSON body (postBodyRaw=true) and a JSONPostProcessor extracting access_token into a variable, followed by a GET /orders sampler with an Authorization: Bearer ${token} header.

assertions.name: well_formed_xml
assertions.text: Output parses as well-formed XML with root <jmeterTestPlan>.

assertions.name: fixed_iterations
assertions.text: ThreadGroup has threads=50, LoopController.loops=200, and scheduler is false (no duration).

assertions.name: raw_json_body
assertions.text: The login sampler uses a single nameless HTTPArgument and HTTPSampler.postBodyRaw=true (not query params).

assertions.name: json_extractor
assertions.text: A JSONPostProcessor extracts access_token (jsonPathExprs $.access_token) into a referenceName.

assertions.name: bearer_header
assertions.text: The orders sampler has an HTTP Header Manager with Authorization: Bearer referencing the extracted variable.

assertions.name: ordering
assertions.text: The login sampler precedes the orders sampler within the same thread group.

evals.prompt: 負荷テストのシナリオを作って。example.org に対して、CSVファイル(user_ids.csv の user_id 列)を使って GET /users/${user_id} を叩く。100ユーザー、3分間、リクエスト間に1〜2秒のランダムな待機を入れて。レスポンスは200を期待。
evals.expected_output: A .jmx with a CSV Data Set Config reading user_ids.csv into user_id, a Thread Group (threads=100, duration=180), a GET /users/${user_id} sampler with a Uniform Random Timer (~1000-2000ms total) and a response_code 200 assertion.

assertions.name: well_formed_xml
assertions.text: Output parses as well-formed XML with root <jmeterTestPlan>.

assertions.name: csv_dataset
assertions.text: A CSVDataSet has filename user_ids.csv and variableNames user_id.

assertions.name: path_variable
assertions.text: The sampler path is /users/${user_id} (variable used in the path, not as a query param).

assertions.name: random_think_time
assertions.text: A UniformRandomTimer is present with delay+range covering roughly 1000-2000 ms.
